key_insight: For Wasserstein-robust linear regression, minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR) achieve minimax regret rates, while standard DRO can be suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors.
engineering_relevance: When regression models face distribution shift, optimizing worst-case excess risk rather than worst-case risk can improve robustness relative to the best predictor for each target distribution.
method: Model source-to-target shift as an adversarial 2-Wasserstein perturbation of radius ε.
Characterize small-shift regret through a problem-specific condition number κ.
Develop an exact convex reformulation for MRO and an accelerated proximal algorithm for SNR.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical minimax-rate results, high-probability finite-sample guarantees, and numerical experiments separating MRO and SNR performance from DRO.
watch_item: The results concern multivariate least-squares regression under Wasserstein-bounded shifts; the abstract does not establish applicability to other losses or shift models.
